title: Your brain studies while you sleep
summary: Sleep helps consolidate memories: the brain replays and strengthens some of what you learned during the day. Cutting sleep to study can backfire.
evidenceNote: Sleep's role in memory is well supported. Exactly how each sleep stage contributes is still actively researched — the stage-by-stage picture here is simplified.

scenes.text: Sleep isn't downtime for your brain.
While you sleep, your brain replays and strengthens some of what you learned during the day.
Different stages seem to do different jobs.

items.title: Deep sleep
items.detail: Linked to consolidating facts and events

items.title: REM sleep
items.detail: Linked to emotional memories and some skills

scenes.text: Health authorities recommend that adults get at least 7 hours of sleep a night.
